issues.legal_issue: An executing court must adjudicate an independent claim to immovable property raised by a person resisting delivery of possession, and cannot reject that claim solely because related proceedings were previously decided where those proceedings do not bind the claimant.
material_facts: The appellant resisted execution, asserting an independent right and possession in land he claimed was distinct from the properties covered by the possession decree.
The appellant was not a party to the possession suit or appeal, and the earlier writ proceedings recorded no adverse finding or relief against his father.
The executing court rejected the objection as already decided in earlier proceedings without adjudicating the appellant’s independent claim.
issues.conclusion: The executing court was required to adjudicate the independent claim under the execution procedure. The earlier proceedings did not justify refusing that adjudication, and the matter was remitted to the executing court.
issues.legal_principle: Order 21 Rules 97, 98, 100, 101, 103 and 104 of the Code of Civil Procedure require the executing court to determine relevant questions of right, title or interest raised in proceedings resisting or complaining of dispossession. The determination has the force of a decree and is appealable; a separate suit is not the prescribed means of resolving the claim. The 1976 amendment removed the former separate-suit remedy under Order 21 Rule 103 of the 1908 Code. The procedure is intended to provide effective adjudication and shorten execution litigation. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and independent_property_claim and claimant_in_possession and no_binding_adverse_determination

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A person in possession applies during execution of a possession decree to resist delivery of immovable property.
predicates.independent_property_claim: The person claims a right, title, or interest in the disputed property independently of the judgment-debtor.
predicates.claimant_in_possession: The person asserting the independent claim is in possession of the disputed property.
predicates.no_binding_adverse_determination: Earlier proceedings neither bound the claimant through an adverse determination nor decided the claimant’s asserted right against them.

issues.definition: When a person in possession raises an independent property claim in an execution obstruction proceeding and no binding adverse determination has already decided that claim, the executing court must adjudicate it.

issues.legal_issue: When an independent property claim concerns land that may lie outside the property described in the decree, adjudication must be confined to whether the claimed land is included in the decree property, without reopening final determinations of the decree property’s boundaries or extent.
material_facts: The possession decree concerned two identified properties, while the appellant claimed a separate parcel that he said had not vested in the custodian or been sold to the respondent.
Whether the claimed parcel formed part of the properties covered by the decree had not been determined.
The appellant had made no claim to the properties covered by the final sale certificates.
issues.conclusion: The only issue for the executing court was whether the claimed parcel was part of the properties covered by the decree and, if it was not, whether execution could reach it. The final boundaries and extent of the properties covered by the sale certificates were not to be reopened; the court could appoint a commissioner to demarcate the properties.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 21 Rules 97, 98 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the executing court determines the questions relevant to the obstruction claim. That adjudication must address the actual property dispute, while respecting matters already final and not claimed by the objector. The court may use a commissioner to assist with demarcation where property identity is disputed.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and independent_property_claim and claimed_land_may_fall_outside_decree_property and property_identity_unresolved and decree_property_extent_final

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A person raises an objection to delivery of immovable property during execution of a possession decree.
predicates.independent_property_claim: The objector claims an independent right, title, or interest in land.
predicates.claimed_land_may_fall_outside_decree_pro: The objector asserts that the land claimed is separate from the land covered by the decree.
predicates.property_identity_unresolved: It remains undetermined whether the claimed land is included in the property covered by the decree.
predicates.decree_property_extent_final: The boundaries or extent of the property covered by the decree have already been finally determined.

issues.definition: If an execution objection concerns independent land that may lie outside the decree property, its identity is unresolved, and the decree property’s extent is final, the court determines only whether the claimed land is included in the decree property.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s possession of property claimed independently must be protected while the executing court adjudicates the obstruction claim.
material_facts: The appellant asserted possession of the disputed parcel under an independent claim.
The executing court had not yet determined whether that parcel formed part of the property covered by the decree.
issues.conclusion: The appellant’s possession was to be protected by interim orders pending adjudication of the claim.
issues.legal_principle: The scheme of Order 21 Rules 97, 98 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires adjudication of the obstruction claim before its final resolution. The court should preserve possession in the interregnum on the factual circumstances so that execution does not cause injustice before the claimant’s right is determined.

rule.if: execution_obstruction_proceeding and claimant_in_possession and independent_property_claim and claim_pending_adjudication

predicates.execution_obstruction_proceeding: A person resists delivery of immovable property during execution of a possession decree.
predicates.claimant_in_possession: The person asserting the claim is in possession of the disputed property.
predicates.independent_property_claim: The person asserts a right, title, or interest in the property independently of the judgment-debtor.
predicates.claim_pending_adjudication: The executing court has not yet determined the person’s claim.

issues.definition: When a person in possession raises an independent claim during execution and that claim remains undecided, the person’s possession is protected until adjudication.
